title: Lost and Found - Stories with Rory #1
topic: Lost and Found - Stories with Rory #1

qa.q: Describe an occasion when you lost something and then you got it back.
qa.a: Well, I'm not usually a forgetful person. In fact, I actually like everything in its place. But there was this really bad time when I was on holiday in Israel. It was about four or five years ago. Uh, I'd gone there to celebrate just being promoted to a managerial role. The plan was to go to Israel, and then after that to come back to Russia, after being in the UK for the summer. Um, so I thought I would just take a small holiday and celebrate. Um, we were, it was the second day, and I was sitting on the terrace, partying and talking to people, and then I suddenly realized that I didn't have my passport. I usually kept it in my back pocket, but when I checked for it, it wasn't there. So I, I panicked. It was awful. It was a terrible feeling. Um, and we spent the next hour looking around, trying to find it, but we couldn't find it there. It was one of the worst feelings ever. Obviously, when you're in a foreign country, your passport is quite important because you needed it to move around places, and I needed mine to go and, well, go to Russia after I was finished in Israel. But, um, it just, it wasn't there. So it was almost a complete disaster. In addition to that, I'd also got all the stamps in there from all the places that I'd been to beforehand. So it had a lot of memories attached to it. Anyway, I did get it back, but only after I'd canceled the passport. Um, I got it back under really embarrassing circumstances, actually. Um, the cleaner found it a couple of days later when she was, uh, well, just cleaning, I suppose. And she came up to me and she was so happy that she'd found it. But I groaned and moaned because it was completely useless now. I couldn't use it to keep traveling onward to Russia, because I'd canceled it, and I had to go back to get a new one. Um, so, even though I got it back, you know, there were still problems as a result. However, it wasn't a complete loss. I still got my passport back and I still had all my memories in it, but it was quite a bad experience.

qa.q: How long was it? How long was the whole [holiday]?
qa.a: I think it was about a week, five days. It wasn't a very long holiday, but it was the most stressful holiday I've ever had.

qa.q: When exactly did you lose your passport? Like, on the first day?
qa.a: No, no. Um, it was the second night. I remember it very clearly. I know it was the second night, um, because I'd had a great time, like, on the first night.

qa.q: What were you wearing that night?
qa.a: Um, to be honest, the same things I always wear when I'm on holiday in a hot country, just like a t-shirt and shorts and sandals.

qa.q: So your shorts had a back pocket?
qa.a: Yes. They're like cargo shorts.

qa.q: Before you actually realized that, um, there was no passport in your pocket, what had you been doing before that?
qa.a: Well, the thing is, I was just speaking to people because I wasn't, I didn't really like drink any alcohol on holiday at all, so it wasn't like I got drunk or something. I was just clumsy and misplaced the damn thing.

qa.q: So you were walking on the beach or, like, you were in a cafe when you kind of, when you did realize that, oh, where's my passport?
qa.a: We were, we were sitting on the terrace. There were a lot of people. A terrace is like an open area, um, or at least in this case, it was an open area on the top floor of the hostel.

qa.q: Do you always, uh, carry your passports in your freaking pocket?
qa.a: Well, I used to, but now every time I go on holiday, I make sure I put it in a safe or something like that where it's safe, even from me.

qa.q: When you realized that there was no passport, what exactly did you do?
qa.a: Well, panicked, basically. Because it was the middle of the night, so there was nothing that could be done, really. Um, after I was finished panicking, we looked around for a while, but we couldn't find it. So we just decided to forget it, keep having fun, and then we'll try and fix the problem the next day.

qa.q: So you, like, kept on going? Kept having fun?
qa.a: Well, there's nothing to do. I mean, if you try and fix a problem, but you can't in the initial stages, and everything else you do is just repeating the same thing again and again. You're not really doing much to help your mental state, are you? So why bother?

qa.q: What about your friends? What did they say?
qa.a: Oh, they were about as horrified as I was.

qa.q: What did you feel the instant when you realized that you'd lost your passport?
qa.a: Like I say, it was like the world had ended. Um, like my stomach dropped, like the bottom of my stomach dropped out. The world kind of turned, uh, the gravity kind of shifted, at least that's what it felt like. It was a really terrible experience.

qa.q: So the next day, you went, um, to the embassy or to the kind of visa center in Israel and applied for a new passport?
qa.a: Well, the next day, I, um, called the passport office in the UK and they canceled the original passport. Um, this means if it was stolen, then it was useless. And then the following day after that, I arranged to pick up a replacement passport and go back to the UK. And then I would get my new one. Um, so it wasn't a total disaster, but it was really annoying because it meant I had to wait another two weeks to go to Russia and start working.

qa.q: So you had to go from Israel back to the UK, right? To get the passport?
qa.a: Uh, yeah, it was a direct flight.

qa.q: And did they tell you that they'd going to give you some paper or some, like, temporary thing?
qa.a: Yep, I got a temporary passport. It was white, um, and it looks really different from the usual passport. It's like very, uh, white and light and flimsy.

qa.q: When did you get your passport back from this lady?
qa.a: Um, like I say, on the second day, just after I'd, um, not the second day of me being there, the second day of this whole crisis. So, I got it back just after I'd canceled my old passport, basically, which was, it was so frustrating and just so ironic.

qa.q: And what did you do? So you got your passport back, and what, you canceled the canceling of the old passport?
qa.a: I tried, but once the process has started, you can't stop it.

qa.q: So you did fly back to Moscow, and then you flew back to the UK to get a new passport?
qa.a: No, no, I had to fly back to the UK. Um, I couldn't fly to Moscow because my, my visa was, um, completely invalid as well at that point.

qa.q: Where did the lady, the hostel lady find your passport?
qa.a: Under a chair.

qa.q: Did you have a nice holiday in Israel?
qa.a: It was a good holiday. Like, apart from that one incident, it was actually one of the best holidays, but it was just really, um, that kind of cast a, a dark cloud over everything.

qa.q: And after that story, um, have you ever lost any passports? Yours or any anyone else's?
qa.a: No, no, you can't. Um, in the UK, I think you can only lose your passport two or three times, and then they just refuse to give you another one.

qa.q: So Maria, what do you think? Is it the truth or is it a lie?
qa.a: Well, you did answer all of my questions and you were pretty detailed in the story, and actually, I see this happening, you know, like you were having fun with your mates, okay, at night, somewhere in Israel in a hostel, um, and then, kind of, you were wearing these shorts. But usually, kind of, you are so well-organized. I like to think this is why I'm so well-organized because bad things kept happening when I was not well-organized. Yeah, because I know, like, you're a super well-organized person, and you, kind of, you write everything down, and you put, I'm sure you put things in the proper places. Okay, I'm going to go for, I think it's true, it's a true story. And then maybe after that, you, yeah, as you say, like, you've become even more organized. It is true, yay! Victory! Woohoo! Yes, five points for Maria. It is true, of course it's true.
